title: Exact chordal separation of spherical Fibonacci points
description:
This research note proves the exact finite separation conjecture stated in Johann S. Brauchart's OWR 40/2012 contribution, published in 2013. For every integer n at least 3, the rational unshifted unit-sphere configuration with Fn points has minimum Euclidean chord 2/sqrt(Fn), uniquely at the north pole and its first latitude point. A latitude-longitude inequality reduces the all-pair lower bound to classical Fibonacci dual-lattice arithmetic. An elementary unimodular-basis proof of the weaker arithmetic bound needed here makes the argument self-contained. The older construction, pole upper bound and Zaremba product index are credited. The theorem does not assert optimal sphere packing or apply to midpoint, irrational-angle or arbitrary-cardinality variants.

Two independent extensive bounded primary-source priority audits identified no earlier exact resolution in the sources inspected. This is not a worldwide first-priority guarantee or a certificate of openness in 2026. The in-preparation Brauchart-Dick item's fate, original Hannay-Nye PDF/version authentication, the full 2015 graphics mapping body, and some final graphics/citation/version coverage remain unverified. The supporting priority note records the actual scope and limits.

The verification archive contains the standalone manuscript source, an unchanged original proof, unchanged author and independent rational certificate programs, finite exact unimodular-basis and metric controls, coordinate-identity falsification controls, expected scientific outcomes, a process runner with time deadlines and bounded cleanup, provenance and reproduction instructions. Finite computations supplement the analytic proof and do not certify an infinite theorem or novelty. AI tools were used extensively for derivation, literature comparison, computation, reproduction, writing and independent adversarial verification. This is an unrefereed preprint with no human peer review or proof-assistant certificate.
